findings.title: Unattached EBS volume
findings.detail: 200 GiB gp2 (old-jenkins-data), not attached to any instance
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the owner, snapshot it (cheap insurance), then delete the volume. The command waits for the snapshot to finish (up to 10 minutes); if the wait times out, delete the volume once the snapshot shows 'completed'. Delete the snapshot too after a month or two if nobody needs it.
findings.fix_command: SNAP=$(aws ec2 create-snapshot --region ap-south-1 --volume-id vol-021fe5f4debe2e734 --description 'billdoctor: backup before delete' --query SnapshotId --output text) && aws ec2 wait snapshot-completed --region ap-south-1 --snapshot-ids "$SNAP" && aws ec2 delete-volume --region ap-south-1 --volume-id vol-021fe5f4debe2e734

findings.title: Old snapshot not used by any AMI
findings.detail: 410 days old, from a 200 GiB volume. pre-migration backup 2025
findings.recommendation: Keep only what your retention policy needs (e.g. 30-90 days) - set up Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager instead of manual snapshots. Saving shown is an upper bound (snapshots are incremental).
findings.fix_command: aws ec2 delete-snapshot --region ap-south-1 --snapshot-id snap-623da09cda0b9887a

findings.title: Elastic IP not associated
findings.detail: 127.184.176.136 is not attached to anything
findings.recommendation: Release it unless an allow-list somewhere depends on this exact IP.

findings.title: Instance stopped for a long time
findings.detail: t3.large (old-build-agent) stopped for 75 days, 1 volume(s) attached
findings.recommendation: If it is not coming back: create an AMI (keeps a restorable copy), then terminate the instance. Volumes with 'delete on termination' turned off survive the termination; delete them too (the AMI holds a copy) or they show up as unattached volumes next time.
findings.fix_command: IMG=$(aws ec2 create-image --region ap-south-1 --instance-id i-8891acb15ab0eabd4 --name billdoctor-i-8891acb15ab0eabd4 --query ImageId --output text) && aws ec2 wait image-available --region ap-south-1 --image-ids "$IMG" && aws ec2 terminate-instances --region ap-south-1 --instance-ids i-8891acb15ab0eabd4

findings.title: Instance looks idle
findings.detail: t2.large (legacy-reporting): average CPU 2.7%, peak 7.5% over 13 days
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the owner. Then stop it, schedule it (office hours only), or downsize. Saving shown assumes it can be stopped.
findings.fix_command: aws ec2 stop-instances --region ap-south-1 --instance-ids i-1222cd8a252d8edc1

findings.title: Previous-generation instance type
findings.detail: t2.large -> t3.large
findings.recommendation: Change the instance type to t3.large during a maintenance window (stop, change type, start). Newer types run on Nitro: very old AMIs need the ENA and NVMe drivers (current images have them). A stop/start changes the public IP unless it is an Elastic IP. Graviton (t4g/m7g) is cheaper still if the software runs on ARM.
findings.fix_command: aws ec2 stop-instances --region ap-south-1 --instance-ids i-1222cd8a252d8edc1 && aws ec2 wait instance-stopped --region ap-south-1 --instance-ids i-1222cd8a252d8edc1 && aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute --region ap-south-1 --instance-id i-1222cd8a252d8edc1 --instance-type Value=t3.large && aws ec2 start-instances --region ap-south-1 --instance-ids i-1222cd8a252d8edc1

findings.title: Load balancer has no targets
findings.detail: application load balancer with 1 target group(s) and 0 registered targets
findings.recommendation: Delete it if the service is gone. First check DNS records pointing at it, and its listener rules: a load balancer without targets can still serve redirects or fixed responses.
findings.fix_command: aws elbv2 delete-load-balancer --region ap-south-1 --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:ap-south-1:123456789012:loadbalancer/app/old-promo-alb/3eacd4314c9ad45d

findings.title: Log group keeps data forever
findings.detail: 12.00 GB stored, retention: never expire
findings.recommendation: Set a retention period that matches your needs (e.g. 30 days for app logs, longer for audit logs). Saving depends on how old the data is, so it is not estimated.
findings.fix_command: aws logs put-retention-policy --region ap-south-1 --log-group-name '/aws/lambda/old-report-fn' --retention-in-days 30

findings.title: NAT gateway barely used
findings.detail: moved 0.51 GB (in + out) in 14 days (VPC vpc-0527c2ef9d79f9cd3)
findings.recommendation: Delete it if private subnets do not need the internet; use VPC endpoints for S3/DynamoDB/ECR, or public subnets with tight security groups for small dev setups.
findings.fix_command: aws ec2 delete-nat-gateway --region ap-south-1 --nat-gateway-id nat-95a718f3d35a4e2d8

findings.title: Database has had no connections
findings.detail: db.t3.medium postgres 100 GiB: 0 connections in 13 days
findings.recommendation: Take a final snapshot and delete it (stopping only lasts 7 days before AWS restarts it).
findings.fix_command: aws rds delete-db-instance --region ap-south-1 --db-instance-identifier analytics-copy --final-db-snapshot-identifier analytics-copy-billdoctor-final

findings.title: Bucket lifecycle gaps
findings.detail: incomplete multipart uploads are never cleaned up; versioning is on but old versions never expire
findings.recommendation: Add a lifecycle rule: abort incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days and expire noncurrent versions after 30-90 days.
findings.fix_command: aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --region ap-south-1 --bucket acme-uploads-demo --lifecycle-configuration '{"Rules":[{"ID":"billdoctor-hygiene","Status":"Enabled","Filter":{},"AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload":{"DaysAfterInitiation":7},"NoncurrentVersionExpiration":{"NoncurrentDays":60}}]}'  # WARNING: replaces existing rules - merge them first
